# scplotter to work with 10x Xenium data prepared by Giotto[¶](#scplotter-to-work-with-10x-Xenium-data-prepared-by-Giotto)

# scplotter to work with 10x Xenium data prepared by Giotto[¶](#scplotter-to-work-with-10x-Xenium-data-prepared-by-Giotto)

**The technology.** Xenium is an imaging-based platform: a targeted gene
panel is probed in situ and transcripts are detected optically, each one
resolved at subcellular coordinates. Alongside the transcript table the
instrument produces multi-channel morphology images (DAPI and protein
channels) that Giotto can carry as large images, so one object supports
both expression and histology views.

**What this notebook covers.** Creating the object from a Xenium output
directory, separating negative-control and unassigned codewords into
their own feature types, attaching the morphology images, filtering and
normalising, PCA/UMAP and Leiden clustering, and then the scplotter
repertoire: `SpatDimPlot` over images, `SpatFeaturePlot` on cell
metrics, `CellStatPlot`, and `FeatureStatPlot` across marker genes. A
final section aggregates cells onto a pseudo-Visium grid to show the
same tissue at bin resolution.

**Data.** The 10x Xenium workshop bundle (mini morphology plus
transcripts), with the cell and nucleus boundaries shipped by the
instrument.

**Before you run.** A Giotto Python environment, and
`devtools::load_all()` from the package root so the in-development
plotting methods are used.

**Upstream tutorial.**

- <https://giotto-suite.github.io/giotto_workshop_2024/xenium-1.html>

Go back to scplotter documentation:
<https://pwwang.github.io/scplotter/>

    library(Giotto)

    # Ensure Giotto can access a python env
    genv_exists <- suppressMessages(checkGiottoEnvironment())
    print(genv_exists)

    python_path <- Sys.getenv("GIOTTO_PYTHON")
    Sys.setenv(RETICULATE_PYTHON = python_path)

    invisible(capture.output(suppressMessages(set_giotto_python_path(python_path = python_path))))

    # library(scplotter)
    devtools::load_all()

In \[2\]:

    instrs <- createGiottoInstructions(
        save_dir = "data/Xenium_giotto_workshop_results",
        save_plot = FALSE,
        show_plot = TRUE,
        return_plot = TRUE,
        python_path = python_path
    )

    feat_types <- c(
        "rna",
        "UnassignedCodeword",
        "NegControlCodeword",
        "NegControlProbe"
    )
    split_keywords = list(
        c("NegControlProbe"),
        c("UnassignedCodeword"),
        c("NegControlCodeword)"
    ))
    data_path <- "data/Xenium_Giotto_workshop"

    # 4. Create the object
    # If error, remove <data_path>/morphology_focus/morphology_focus_0000.xml
    g <- createGiottoXeniumObject(
        xenium_dir = data_path,
        qv_threshold = 20, # qv of 20 is the default and also what 10x uses
        feat_type = feat_types,
        split_keyword = split_keywords,
        # * if aligned images already converted to .tif, they could be added as named list
        # * instead, see next section
        # load_aligned_images = list(
        #     post_he = c(
        #         "path/to/...he_image.tif",
        #         "path/to/...he_imagealignment.csv"
        #     ),
        #     CD20 = ...,
        #     HER2 = ...,
        #     DAPI = ...
        # ),
        instructions = instrs
    )

    g <- addSpatialCentroidLocations(g, poly_info = "cell")
    g <- addSpatialCentroidLocations(g, poly_info = "nucleus")

    force(g)

In \[3\]:

    # Simple Visualization
    options(repr.plot.width = 8, repr.plot.height = 6)

    SpatDimPlot(
        g,
        image = "black",
        # put shapes at last
        layers = c("image", "points", "shapes"),
        features = head(featIDs(g)),
        shapes_border_color = "cyan",
        shapes_border_size = 0.1,
        shapes_fill_by = "black"
    )

    x <- importXenium(data_path)
    x$filetype$expression <- "mtx" # change to mtx instead of .h5 which is not in the mini dataset

    ex <- x$load_expression()
    featType(ex)

    featType(ex[[2]]) <- c("NegControlProbe")
    featType(ex[[3]]) <- c("NegControlCodeword")
    featType(ex[[4]]) <- c("UnassignedCodeword")
    force(ex)

    g2 <- g
    # append the expression info
    g2 <- setGiotto(g2, ex)

    # load cell metadata
    cx <- x$load_cellmeta()
    g2 <- setGiotto(g2, cx)

    force(g2)

In \[6\]:

    img_paths <- c(
        sprintf("data/Xenium_Giotto_workshop/morphology_focus/morphology_focus_%04d.tif", 0:3),
        "data/Xenium_Giotto_workshop/he_mini.tif"
    )

    img_list <- createGiottoLargeImageList(
        img_paths,
        # naming is based on the channel metadata above
        names = c("DAPI", "18S", "ATP1A1/CD45/E-Cadherin", "alphaSMA/Vimentin", "HE"),
        use_rast_ext = TRUE,
        verbose = FALSE
    )

    # make some images brighter
    img_list[[1]]@max_window <- 5000
    img_list[[2]]@max_window <- 5000
    img_list[[3]]@max_window <- 5000

    # append images to gobject
    g <- setGiotto(g, img_list)

In \[7\]:

    options(repr.plot.width = 12, repr.plot.height = 10)
    p1 <- SpatDimPlot(g, image = "HE", points = FALSE)
    p2 <- SpatDimPlot(g, image = "DAPI", shapes_feat_type = "nucleus", points = FALSE)
    p3 <- SpatDimPlot(g, image = "18S", points = FALSE)
    p4 <- SpatDimPlot(g, image = "ATP1A1/CD45/E-Cadherin", shapes_feat_type = "nucleus",
        points = FALSE)

In \[10\]:

    g <- runPCA(g, feats_to_use = NULL)
    g <- runUMAP(g,
        dimensions_to_use = seq(15),
        n_neighbors = 40 # default
    )
    g <- createNearestNetwork(g,
        dimensions_to_use = seq(15),
        k = 40
    )

    # takes roughly 1 min to run
    g <- doLeidenCluster(g)

    # igraph-based leiden returns integer labels; keep them categorical so that
    # shapes_fill_by / group_by use a discrete scale instead of a continuous one
    g@cell_metadata$cell$rna$leiden_clus <- factor(g@cell_metadata$cell$rna$leiden_clus)

    Setting dimension reduction [cell][rna] pca

    Setting dimension reduction [cell][rna] umap

    As of Giotto 4.2.3 doLeidenCluster() works via {igraph}
     For the python implementation, use doLeidenClusterPython()
     This message appears once per session.

    options(repr.plot.width = 12, repr.plot.height = 6)

    p2 <- CellDimPlot(g, group_by = "leiden_clus", spat_unit = "cell", reduction = "umap")

    options(repr.plot.width = 12, repr.plot.height = 9)

    FeatureStatPlot(
        g,
        features = c(
            "CD3E", "CD8A", "CD4", # T cell
            "MS4A1", # B
            "SFRP2", # CAF (mesenchymal)
            "RAMP2", # endothelial
            "PROX1", # LEC (lymphatic endothelial cell)
            "CPA3", # mast cell
            "MKI67", # epithelial/cancer
            "PDCD1" # PD1
        ),
        layer = "normalized",
        bg_cutoff = 0,  # unexpressed (<=0) cells stay grey instead of taking colour
        upper_quantile = 0.9,
        spat_unit = "cell",
        reduction = "umap",
        plot_type = "dim"
    )

    pvis <- makePseudoVisium(
        extent = ext(g, prefer = c("polygon", "points"), all_data = TRUE),
         # all_data = TRUE is the default
        micron_size = 1
    )

    g <- setGiotto(g, pvis)
    g <- addSpatialCentroidLocations(g, poly_info = "pseudo_visium")
    activeSpatUnit(g) <- "pseudo_visium"

    g <- calculateOverlap(g,
        spatial_info = "pseudo_visium",
        feat_info = "rna"
    )

    g <- overlapToMatrix(g)

    g <- filterGiotto(g,
        expression_threshold = 1,
        feat_det_in_min_cells = 1,
        min_det_feats_per_cell = 100
    )

    g <- normalizeGiotto(g)
    g <- addStatistics(g)
    g <- createSpatialNetwork(g, method = "Delaunay")
